# Last Call: how nightlife works, everywhere

> A cited, independent field guide to nightlife: closing times around the world, the history of going out, last-call laws, how the door works, the money behind a bar or club night, fire codes, safety after dark, dance-floor culture, night mayors and getting home, with Boston as the worked example.

A cited field guide (282 sources, about 33,124 words) to how nightlife works, everywhere: closing times and last-call laws around the world, the history of going out from saloons to Berlin, the door and door policy law, the money behind a night out (door splits, promoters, bottle service, DJ fees), fire codes written after Cocoanut Grove and The Station, staying safe, club culture, the night-time economy and getting home, with Boston as the worked example. Independent.

## Key facts
- What time do bars close in Boston? Boston bars and clubs can serve until 2 a.m. at the latest, because Massachusetts law bans on-premises sales from 2 a.m. to 8 a.m. The Licensing Board sets each license's hours inside that window, so many places close earlier. A temporary 2026 law allowed up to 3 a.m. in opt-in cities, but it expired on July 31, 2026.
- Is last call in Boston 3 a.m. now? No, not as of November 2026. Chapter 96 of the Acts of 2026, signed June 8, 2026, let opt-in cities and towns allow one hour past each license's hours, capped at 3 a.m., through July 31, 2026. In Boston only places already licensed to 2 a.m. could extend, and a permanent 3 a.m. would need the state Legislature.
- What time do bars close in New York City? Up to 4 a.m. New York State bans on-premises service from 4 a.m. to 8 a.m. Monday to Saturday and from 4 a.m. to 10 a.m. on Sunday, the latest default of any large state that sets one. Counties can set earlier hours, and much of upstate does, from 1 a.m. in Ithaca to 3 a.m. in Binghamton.
- Why is happy hour illegal in Massachusetts? Massachusetts banned happy hour in 1984, a push led by the state ABCC chairman and Mothers Against Drunk Driving as a drunk-driving measure. The rule bars free or discounted drinks, unlimited-drink specials, jumbo drinks at a regular drink's price, more than two drinks served to one person at a time and pitchers for fewer than two people.
- Can a bar scan my ID and keep my information? It depends on the state. California limits swiped license data to age and ID checks, legal recordkeeping, check approval and fraud prevention, and Hawaii has limited scanning and keeping it since 2012; New Hampshire allows scanning for alcohol sales only if the scanner stores nothing, per a vendor summary. Research for this guide found no Massachusetts statute limiting ID-scanner data.
- How do club promoters get paid? Common deals include a flat room rental, a door split from the first dollar, expenses off the top then a split, or a guarantee versus a percentage, whichever is greater. Organizers may also take on a bar minimum, and guest-list promoters are often paid per person who shows up, while VIP promoters earn commission on tables.
- Why do exit doors open outward? A crowd pushing toward a door cannot pull it open. After the 1942 Cocoanut Grove fire in Boston, codes required all exit doors to swing outward, along with lit exit signs, emergency lighting and widely separated exits.
- What is Ask for Angela? It is a code phrase: a person who feels unsafe asks bar staff for "Angela" to get discreet help without having to explain. It was created in Lincolnshire, England, in 2016 by Hayley Crawford and has spread to cafes, restaurants and festivals in the UK and abroad, though it only works if staff on shift are trained.
